policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV's 'their little ones' directly renders the qere צְעִירֵיהֶם; the alternative-rendering note 'inferiors' concerns English wording and does not support the ketiv.
ASV's 'a thing of nought' directly renders the qere וֶאֱלִיל, distinguishing it from the ketiv ואלול.
ASV's singular 'the deceit of their own heart' directly renders the qere וְתַרְמִית, distinguishing it from the ketiv ותרמות.
